Evidence: pinned anthropic 0.121.0 already owns a precedence-aware credential chain plus AccessTokenProvider/TokenCache expiry, single-flight refresh, and 401 invalidation; openai 2.53.0 accepts callable keys/provider runtimes/typed workload identity and owns token exchange/cache/refresh; PydanticAI 1.107.2 accepts constructed OpenAI/Anthropic clients; boto3 owns AWS profile/web-identity/container/instance-role discovery and refresh. Airflow universal-secret precedence/collision complexity and keyring headless/pluggable-backend behavior are warnings against copying a universal broker into Rebar.

Recommended candidate (NOT YET APPROVED): non-secret immutable config snapshots; official SDK/client/helper auth by default; typed injection of constructed clients/providers/auth objects for Python; narrowly typed static credentials materialized only at the Jira/Gerrit/Jenkins/etc. adapter that requires them; no universal get_secret()->str, automatic keyring fallback, or built-in cloud secret-manager in core. Rebar still owns fail-closed mechanism selection, expected host/account policy, redacted provenance, lifecycle docs, and leakage prevention.

Concrete current defect: _bridge_runner copies the full parent environment to the reconciler child and then to ticket delivery, so delivery receives unrelated Jira/LLM/cloud credentials. RP-04 must replace this with an adapter-owned baseline plus only the selected auth capability. MCP schemas/arguments must never accept raw credentials or allow a lower-trust caller to select a stronger server identity. Environment rotation in a long-lived process requires restart unless an official provider refreshes or a mounted file is explicitly re-read; no universal hot-rotation promise.

Provider/environment matrix covers Bedrock, OpenAI, Anthropic, Gerrit, GitHub, GitLab, Jenkins, Jira Cloud/DC across local, GitHub Actions, Jenkins, AWS-hosted, CLI, library, MCP, and hosted-service use. Primary sources and later verification obligations are cited in the artifact. No production code, ADR, epic, or implementation stories were created.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: Concrete RP-04 composition sketch added to .joe-janitor/rp04-secrets-research.md. The proposed seam is one immutable non-secret OperationSnapshot composed at runtime with separate GitRuntime, LLMRuntime, and selected BridgeRuntime capabilities; it is not a universal secret provider or credential union. Git delegates to credential helpers, SSH agents, or AWS-native remote helpers through a constrained runner environment. LLM provider-specific factories accept boto3, Anthropic, or OpenAI native auth capabilities while Rebar retains retry, timeout, cache, output-contract, and lifecycle policy. Each bridge factory accepts only its provider-specific client/auth shape; static Jira or Jenkins material is revealed only inside that adapter or its exact child environment. Operations instantiate only the runtimes they need, explicit auth selection fails closed without ambient or anonymous fallback, and lifecycle ownership follows client construction ownership. Open design decision: whether the public Python seam initially permits whole-client/runner replacement, which can bypass Rebar transport invariants, or only native auth-provider injection into Rebar-owned factories.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: Maintainer intent clarified and recorded: RP-04 is not an authentication, credential-resolution, storage, or refresh subsystem. Rebar is a safe provider-integration host. Upstream SDKs/helpers/CI/deployments own issuance, retrieval, persistence, refresh, rotation, invalidation, and precedence. Rebar owns only safe passage through its seams: fail-closed provider selection, trusted typed provider bindings, operation-scoped construction, exclusion from snapshots/caches/fingerprints/tickets/MCP/CLI/logs/errors, subprocess and adapter isolation, narrow unwrapping of unavoidable static values at the sending adapter, native lifecycle preservation, construction-based close ownership, and non-secret host/account/project policy. The research artifact now uses provider/integration binding as the umbrella concept; RuntimeBindings is explicitly not a credential broker.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: Added a Pydantic-ecosystem comparison and end-to-end environment traces. PydanticAI supports API-key shortcuts but also direct injection of official OpenAI, Anthropic, and boto3 clients; Rebar should use client injection so Pydantic validates only the non-secret operation snapshot while the official SDK owns auth. FastAPI/Pydantic Settings and Instructor confirm the common environment-at-process-boundary convention. Local: shell or external tooling exports the provider variable; the Rebar-owned SDK factory consumes the native environment chain and injects the client into PydanticAI. GitHub Actions: the workflow maps a GitHub secret only onto the Rebar step environment; the same SDK path runs, no GitHub Secrets API or raw CLI secret is involved, and missing fork/Dependabot secrets fail closed. AWS SSM Parameter Store: ECS or deployment bootstrap maps SecureString to the provider env variable using the task execution role; Rebar does not call SSM. Bedrock instead uses the task role through boto3 with no stored API key. AWS confirms ECS environment injection is start-time only, so rotation requires a new task/forced deployment. A host application may alternatively retrieve SSM and inject a constructed client, retaining retrieval/rotation ownership. Gitleaks found no leaks after recording the research.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: APPROVED RP-04 decision: static-secret rotation for long-running processes is restart/redeploy based. Short-lived CLI processes receive current startup environment; long-running MCP/server processes must restart after a static secret changes; container workloads must restart/redeploy so the platform reinjects the current value, including ECS new-task/forced-deployment behavior. Rebar will not poll environment, retrieve/refresh SSM, watch secret files, or maintain a hot-reload secret cache. If the old credential is revoked before restart, operations fail as authentication failures without fallback to another ambient or anonymous identity. Native temporary/workload credentials remain SDK-owned and may refresh in process. Added implementation verification obligations for new process, long-running process, post-restart, revoked old credential, and native refresh cases. Gitleaks found no leaks.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: Subprocess-environment research revised the prior strict-allowlist recommendation. Full inheritance is standard for ordinary trusted same-principal subprocesses and has not been community-rejected: Python subprocess defaults to inheritance; pip copies os.environ then offers targeted extra_environ/unset_environ; pre-commit defaults to inherited env; GitHub Actions overlays a step environment; Jenkins scopes credential env to a build block and descendants. Strict filtering appears at deliberate hermetic/reproducibility boundaries such as tox pass_env/disallow_pass_env and Bazel action/repository environments. A global or adapter allowlist in Rebar would be fragile across Git helpers, SSH agents, AWS credential_process, proxy/CA, runtime, and platform variables. The actual Rebar defect is sibling propagation: bridge reconciliation, ACLI, delivery, and detached push reuse broad parent environments. Revised unapproved candidate: preserve ambient inheritance for trusted same-capability children; never mutate global os.environ to install adapter secrets; overlay Rebar-materialized static values only onto their owning child; remove exact Rebar-declared secret variable names when launching an unrelated sibling; preserve unknown ambient/native chains; rely primarily on step/container/service secret scoping; defer strict/hermetic mode. Security claim is limited to Rebar-known credential non-propagation, not sandboxing. Research artifact updated; Gitleaks found no leaks.

## Context / Problem
RP-04 ordinary configuration is approved, but its secrets/authentication design is intentionally unapproved. Rebar must safely support Bedrock, OpenAI, Anthropic, Gerrit, GitHub, GitLab, Jenkins, Jira Cloud, and Jira Data Center across local developer workstations, GitHub Actions, Jenkins, AWS-hosted services, CLI, library, MCP, and hosted-service consumers. A universal secret broker or hand-rolled credential store could weaken SDK-native refresh, workload identity, credential-helper protection, rotation, and redaction.

## Approach
Remain in architecture RESEARCH and use rebar-brainstorm. Inventory current Rebar credential boundaries and external dependencies. Consult current official documentation/source for each provider and environment, plus mature actively maintained OSS prior art. Produce a provider/environment matrix that identifies credential shape, authoritative mechanism, refresh/rotation owner, injection source, whether Rebar needs raw material, and failure/redaction obligations. Critically compare a generic secret-provider abstraction against typed capability/provider seams and direct delegation to official SDK/helper chains. Record constraints separately from Rebar-owned choices. No ADR, epic, implementation tickets, or production changes until the maintainer confirms the written findings and approves the design through dialogue.

## Scope
Read-only repository, tracker, dependency-source, and web research. Checkout-local ignored findings live at `.joe-janitor/rp04-secrets-research.md`; durable conclusions are commented here. Never read `~/.zshrc`, disclose credentials, invoke secrets through argv, or persist raw credentials.

## Verification
Cross-check official mechanisms against current Rebar call sites and at least several mature OSS implementations. Every matrix claim cites a current primary source where available. Identify unsupported or ambiguous cases explicitly rather than inventing a credential protocol. Audit the written artifact for absence of secret values and for coverage of all named providers and environments.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The written dependency findings cover all named providers and environments, cite what was consulted, state actual credential/refresh behavior, and distinguish external constraints from Rebar-owned choices.
- [ ] A provider/environment matrix records credential shape, preferred authoritative mechanism, refresh/rotation ownership, local/CI/AWS-hosted source, raw-secret exposure, and fail-safe behavior.
- [ ] Mature actively maintained OSS prior art is compared, including how projects delegate to SDK chains, credential helpers, workload identity, CI credential binding, keyrings, or external secret managers.
- [ ] The research critically evaluates universal string lookup, typed credential/provider capabilities, direct ambient delegation, subprocess handoff, library injection, MCP/CLI trust boundaries, redaction, and rotation.
- [ ] `.joe-janitor/rp04-secrets-research.md` is read back, contains no credential values, and is summarized durably on this ticket.
- [ ] The maintainer receives exactly one evidence-backed RP-04 secrets decision question; no ADR, epic, child stories, or production code are created in this phase.
